# gtk4's own widgets are sngl:platform/gtk4's (widgets.sngl, from the bundled
# GIR), which a program names as `gtk4.GtkProgressBar`. A program may instead
# import `gir:Gtk-4.0`, the gir: scheme's package -- a library plugin,
# lib/x/scheme/gir -- declared from the GIR the `gir` option selects, against
# the platform's Look and `setLook`. Its classes have no wrapper, so a Go
# program calls their C itself.

# The platform package checks on its own.
sngl check sngl:platform/gtk4

# A program reaches a widget, and a GIR action on it, through the import, in
# both languages: Go through the platform's wrappers, C directly.
sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --opt gir=builtin --out=out app.sngl
grep 'cgo\.GtkProgressBarPulse' out/main.go
sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=c --opt gir=builtin --out=outc app.sngl
grep 'gtk_progress_bar_pulse' outc/main.c

# The platform's own widget, and its action, through the wrapper.
sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --out=own own.sngl
grep 'cgo\.GtkProgressBarPulse' own/main.go

-- app.sngl --
import gtk "gir:Gtk-4.0"
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

ui.window {
    gtk.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}
    time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick { bar.pulse() })
}
-- own.sngl --
import gtk4 "sngl:platform/gtk4"
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

ui.window {
    gtk4.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}
    time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick { bar.pulse() })
}
